name: General Knowledge
description: Foundational GK for any competitive exam: science, geography, India and the world.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet — roughly 11 times Earth's diameter and more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

questions.question: Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana' in Bengali; it was adopted as the national anthem in 1950. Bankim Chandra wrote 'Vande Mataram'.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is India's longest river. The Godavari is the longest river flowing entirely within India.

questions.question: Who was the first President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the first President from 1950 to 1962 — the only President elected to two full terms.

questions.question: Which is the smallest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Goa (~3,702 km²) is the smallest state by area; Sikkim is second-smallest.

questions.question: What is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The Royal Bengal Tiger has been India's national animal since 1973, when Project Tiger was launched.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution's Drafting Committee and is regarded as its principal architect.

questions.question: Which Indian city is famously known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is India's top IT and startup hub, earning it the 'Silicon Valley of India' title.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali' — the first Indian laureate.

questions.question: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: Japan uses the Yen (¥). Yuan is China's currency, Won is Korea's, and Ringgit is Malaysia's.

questions.question: Which country is the most populous in the world (as of 2023–24)?
questions.explanation: According to UN estimates, India overtook China as the world's most populous country in April 2023.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Gold's symbol is Au, from the Latin 'aurum'. Ag is silver, Gd is gadolinium, Pb is lead.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest (8,849 m) in the Himalayas is the world's highest peak; K2 is second.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about a third of the Earth's surface — larger than all land area combined.

questions.question: What is the national flower of India?
questions.explanation: The Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is India's national flower — a symbol of purity and detachment.

questions.question: Which vitamin is produced in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UV-B sunlight converts a cholesterol derivative in the skin into Vitamin D — hence its 'sunshine vitamin' nickname.

questions.question: How many states does India currently have?
questions.explanation: After the 2019 bifurcation of Jammu & Kashmir, India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra, purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne, became the capital in 1913.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when mould contaminated a petri dish — the world's first antibiotic.

questions.question: The Red Fort is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Red Fort was built by Shah Jahan in Delhi (1639–48); the Prime Minister hoists the flag here on Independence Day.

questions.question: What is the national bird of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian Peacock (Pavo cristatus) was declared the national bird in 1963.

questions.question: Which gas do plants primarily absorb from the atmosphere for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis, using sunlight energy.

questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru served as Prime Minister from 1947 until his death in 1964 — the longest tenure in Indian history.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, is located off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches ~2,300 km along Australia's Queensland coast and is visible from space.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest continent at about 8.6 million km² — though it's the sixth-largest country.

questions.question: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
questions.explanation: Adults have 206 bones. Babies are born with about 300, some of which fuse as they grow.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide (rust) on Mars' surface gives it the reddish colour that earned it the 'Red Planet' name.

questions.question: In which year was the ₹ (Indian Rupee) symbol officially adopted?
questions.explanation: The ₹ symbol, designed by D. Udaya Kumar, was adopted by the Government of India on 15 July 2010.

questions.question: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, heaviest and strongest bone in the human body.

questions.question: Which Indian state is popularly known as 'God's Own Country'?
questions.explanation: Kerala earned the tourism tagline 'God's Own Country' for its backwaters, greenery and beaches.
